originality.rationale: Tian’s Oct. 2026 primary-47B38 paper analyzes weighted Fock products and does not derive fixed-slope singular layers. Sang–Zhao give the same quadratic compactness boundary and operator eigenvectors, not modulus singular values. The oscillator-semigroup study of Dereziński–Karczmarczyk gives general Gaussian polar and norm machinery, hence the geometric subcritical form is not credited as an independently novel method. The joined quantitative claim adds the exact noncompact endpoint essential norm and locally uniform sqrt-distance singular-layer/counted-level asymptotics for this natural fixed-slope family; those are not stated in inspected full-text sources. Priority risk remains if general Gaussian normal forms plus limiting arguments have already been explicitly exploited elsewhere.
residual_risks: Gaussian oscillator-semigroup normal-form theorems may imply the subcritical singular-value formulas as a specialized corollary.
The degree to which an oscillator-semigroup boundary limit plus a compactness criterion would imply the fixed-slope quantitative counting law merits independent priority review.
The full text of Le (2014) was not inspected; only the abstract and accessible recent reproductions of its criteria were available.
No claim is made of exhaustive global publication coverage.
